definitions.meaning: the hunchbacked king was nicknamed for his bent back in Tudor accounts
Guy, the central figure of Evelyn Waugh's Sword of Honour trilogy, bears this surname

explanation.surface: A question whether Shakespeare's villain king could stand as the hero of an Evelyn Waugh novel.
explanation.definitionFit: One surname serves both: a byname for the hump-backed king and the family name of Waugh's wartime protagonist Guy.

definitions.meaning: James M. ... wrote The Postman Always Rings Twice
in Genesis the first killer slew his brother Abel

explanation.surface: The killer in a detective novelist's book.
explanation.definitionFit: The surname of the American hardboiled novelist is also the name of the Biblical son of Adam who killed Abel.

clue.text: Fruitful burning issue in Mackay book

definitions.text: Fruitful burning issue in Mackay book

parts.words: Fruitful burning issue in Mackay book
parts.note: Shena Mackay's novel is titled The ___ on Fire: a fruit-bearing place that is literally a burning matter

explanation.surface: A hot topic raised in a book by Shena Mackay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Burning issue' reads as a hot topic, but it points to the title The Orchard on Fire, where the fruit trees are what burns.
explanation.definitionFit: A plot of fruit trees is the fruitful place set alight in the title of Shena Mackay's novel.

clue.text: Faculty of Mrs Erdleigh which allowed her to anticipate re-entry into the "Vortex of 4"

definitions.text: Faculty of Mrs Erdleigh which allowed her to anticipate re-entry into the "Vortex of 4"

parts.words: Faculty of Mrs Erdleigh which allowed her to anticipate re-entry into the "Vortex of 4"
parts.note: Mrs Erdleigh is the fortune-teller in Anthony Powell's A Dance to the Music of Time, who foresees future events

explanation.surface: A character's special gift lets her foresee a return to some mystic vortex.
explanation.definitionFit: The gift of foreseeing events is second sight, which Powell's fortune-teller Mrs Erdleigh possesses.

clue.text: Developing into a work by Martin du Gard

definitions.text: a work by Martin du Gard
definitions.meaning: Roger Martin du Gard's early novel Devenir! translates to this English title

explanation.surface: Something turning into a book by the French Nobel novelist.
explanation.definitionFit: Growing to be something is the present participle of 'become', and Martin du Gard's novel Devenir! is rendered thus in English.

clue.text: Barrister who lost his head in Paris

definitions.text: Barrister who lost his head in Paris

parts.words: Barrister who lost his head in Paris
parts.note: Sydney, the lawyer in A Tale of Two Cities, goes to the guillotine in Paris in place of Darnay

explanation.surface: A lawyer who panicked while visiting France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lost his head' suggests panic, but Dickens's Sydney Carton is literally guillotined in Paris.
explanation.definitionFit: Sydney, the dissolute advocate of Dickens's A Tale of Two Cities, is beheaded in Paris in another man's place.

indicators.note: the words Iago, not Othello feature the answer within their letters, running across the comma

explanation.surface: A festival presenting Shakespeare's villain rather than the Moor.
explanation.definitionFit: In ancient Greece a public contest or festival of games was called by this name.

clue.text: Four kings dealt by Victorian novelist

definitions.text: Four kings dealt by Victorian novelist

parts.words: Four kings dealt by Victorian novelist
parts.note: Thackeray's lectures on the Hanoverian monarchs I to IV were titled The Four ___

explanation.surface: A card-playing writer dealing out four kings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kings dealt' suggests a card hand, but the four Hanoverian monarchs were dealt with in Thackeray's lectures.
explanation.definitionFit: Thackeray's lectures The Four Georges treat the four Hanoverian kings who reigned 1714-1830.

clue.text: Frightens a sort of Hartley work

indicators.note: to sort letters is to rearrange them, so Frightens a is put in a new order

explanation.surface: A ghost story by L. P. Hartley scares the reader.
explanation.definitionFit: Night Fears is the 1924 short-story collection by L. P. Hartley, author of The Go-Between.

parts.note: the second Forsyte Saga novel shares its legal setting with the Chancery court of Dickens's Bleak House

explanation.surface: Galsworthy adding a gloomy wing to his home.
explanation.walkthrough: Dickens's Bleak House centres on a Chancery lawsuit; Galsworthy's In Chancery continues the Forsyte Saga, so it extends the theme.
explanation.definitionFit: Galsworthy's second Forsyte novel takes its title from the Court of Chancery that dominates Dickens's Bleak House.

indicators.note: signals that the word heard spoken is a homophone of the name

parts.note: to obscure is to fog, to cloud over

explanation.surface: A rumoured shadowy figure from a Jules Verne novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Phileas is the hero who goes Around the World in Eighty Days in Verne's novel.

clue.text: He was shown up by well-known Fabian

definitions.text: He was shown up by well-known Fabian

parts.words: He was shown up by well-known Fabian
parts.note: Shaw, a leading Fabian socialist, wrote The Shewing-up of a horse thief in this play

explanation.surface: A man embarrassed by a famous socialist.
explanation.walkthrough: Shaw was a prominent member of the Fabian Society; his play is The Shewing-up of Blanco Posnet.
explanation.definitionFit: The horse-thief title character of Shaw's 1909 play The Shewing-up of Blanco Posnet.

clue.text: How wind stood for Henry's objective

definitions.text: How wind stood for Henry's objective

parts.words: How wind stood for Henry's objective
parts.note: Drayton's Agincourt ballad opens '___ stood the wind for France', France being Henry V's target

explanation.surface: Asking which way the wind blew for a king's campaign.
explanation.walkthrough: Michael Drayton's Ballad of Agincourt begins 'Fair stood the wind for France', France being Henry V's objective.
explanation.definitionFit: A favourable wind is described by this word in Drayton's line about Henry V's crossing to France.

definitions.meaning: a secret flit by night to dodge the rent
Joyce Cary wrote the 1946 novel The ___

explanation.surface: A secret getaway arranged by a man called Cary.
explanation.definitionFit: A 'flit' by night to dodge creditors, and the title of Joyce Cary's novel.

parts.note: Morris West wrote the novel The ___ about a diplomat in Vietnam

explanation.surface: A diplomat representing the Western powers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'West' looks like the Western world, but it is the Australian novelist Morris West.
explanation.definitionFit: Morris West's 1965 novel The Ambassador concerns a diplomatic emissary in Saigon.

definitions.meaning: Updike's 1969 long poem and collection bears this title

explanation.surface: The heart of a poem by John Updike.
explanation.definitionFit: The halfway point is the centre, and Updike's autobiographical poem collection is titled thus.

indicators.note: the letters, or characters, of senile are rearranged to make a new word

explanation.surface: Cutting off an elderly person who has become confused.
explanation.definitionFit: A literary verb meaning to make into an island, cut off, used by Arnold and others.

parts.note: Finish heard spoken sounds like Finnish, so this is a composer from Finland

explanation.surface: Someone heard finishing off a composer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Finish' reads as a verb, but spoken it sounds like Finnish: the composer is from Finland.
explanation.definitionFit: The composer of Finlandia is Finland's most celebrated musician.

indicators.note: only part of the words Cleopatra's champion is used, the run spanning the two

explanation.surface: Cleopatra's champion was partly taught to shoot arrows.
explanation.definitionFit: Roger, tutor to Elizabeth I, wrote Toxophilus, the first English treatise on the longbow.

parts.note: frank means outspoken, candid
E is the street abbreviation for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A frank account of rapture by the French philosopher.
explanation.definitionFit: Candide is the title character of Voltaire's satire, so a work coming from Voltaire.

clue.text: Legendary monster a lot of bull, pace Mary Renault

definitions.text: Legendary monster a lot of bull, pace Mary Renault

parts.words: Legendary monster a lot of bull, pace Mary Renault
parts.note: the half-bull of Crete, though Renault's The King Must Die makes him wholly human

explanation.surface: A myth dismissed as nonsense, with apologies to the novelist Mary Renault.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A lot of bull' means nonsense and also half-bull; 'pace' (with respect to) nods to Renault, whose Theseus finds a man rather than a monster.
explanation.definitionFit: The bull-headed creature of Cretan myth slain by Theseus in the labyrinth.

clue.text: He was expected to lose weight in court

definitions.text: He was expected to lose weight in court

parts.words: He was expected to lose weight in court
parts.note: Shylock's bond would cut a pound of flesh from this merchant at the Venetian trial

explanation.surface: A man facing a trial where he was due to slim down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lose weight' suggests dieting, but in The Merchant of Venice the merchant owes Shylock a pound of his flesh.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's merchant of Venice pledged a pound of flesh to Shylock, enforced at trial.

indicators.note: in a down entry one piece placed on another sits above it, here the goddess placed relative to the abbreviation

parts.note: Hebe was cup-bearer to the gods on Olympus

explanation.surface: A writer serving a waitress on credit.
explanation.definitionFit: Chinua, the Nigerian author of Things Fall Apart.

clue.text: One of Blake's was a matter of experience

definitions.text: One of Blake's was a matter of experience

parts.words: One of Blake's was a matter of experience
parts.note: Blake's Songs of Innocence and of Experience form linked sets of lyric poems

explanation.surface: Blake learnt one thing through what he had lived.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A matter of experience' sounds like learning through life, but it points to Blake's Songs of Experience.
explanation.definitionFit: A linked group of songs or lyric poems, as Blake's Songs of Experience are.

parts.note: Larry Niven co-wrote with Pournelle the novel ___ of Fealty, a pledge of loyalty

explanation.surface: David Niven turning out a faithful film.
explanation.walkthrough: Larry Niven, the science-fiction writer, not the actor David: his novel with Jerry Pournelle is Oath of Fealty.
explanation.definitionFit: A pledge of fealty is a solemn vow of loyalty, as in Niven and Pournelle's title.

indicators.note: dual means twofold, so the piece appears twice

parts.note: the verb 'is' expresses existence

explanation.surface: A god leads a double life at Oxford.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at Oxford' adds a second sense: the Thames is called the Isis where it flows through Oxford.
explanation.definitionFit: The Egyptian goddess of magic and motherhood, wife of Osiris.

clue.text: The platform is Dali's, without his pupil

indicators.note: without means lacking, so a letter is taken away

parts.note: the painter's name with its possessive
L stands for learner, a pupil

explanation.surface: Salvador Dalí's stage, used without his student.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pupil' looks like part of an eye, apt for a surrealist, but it is L for learner.
explanation.definitionFit: A raised stage at the end of a hall, for speakers or the top table.

clue.text: 'In the — of your months, ye shall blow with the trumpets' (Book of Numbers)

definitions.text: 'In the — of your months, ye shall blow with the trumpets' (Book of Numbers)

parts.words: 'In the — of your months, ye shall blow with the trumpets' (Book of Numbers)
parts.note: a fill-in quotation from Numbers 10:10 in the King James Bible, the gap being the starts of the months

explanation.surface: A Bible verse about sounding trumpets at the start of each month.
explanation.definitionFit: The starts or openings of the months, when the Israelites were to sound trumpets.

indicators.note: return means turn back, so the word for game is read backwards

parts.note: deer are hunted as game

explanation.surface: A poet comes back from hunting.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry, the war poet of Naming of Parts.

clue.text: Sonnets, as I modified, expressed feelings

indicators.note: modified means changed, so the letters of Sonnets as I are reworked

explanation.surface: A poet revising sonnets to convey emotions.
explanation.definitionFit: Physical or emotional perceptions, impressions felt.
